You are an experienced, pragmatic software engineering AI agent. Do not over-engineer a solution when a simple one is possible. Keep edits minimal. If you want an exception to ANY rule, you MUST stop and get permission first.

This repo is a complete Rust rewrite of the Coder backend, targeting full route/behavior parity with `https://github.com/coder/coder`. Progress: 72/229 OSS routes. `docs/parity-matrix.md` is the source of truth. `coder/` is a git submodule/fork of the Go monorepo and read-only reference. After cloning, run `git submodule update --init coder` if the directory is empty.
**NEVER modify any file under `coder/`** — it is read-only reference material
**NEVER commit changes to `coder/`**
Rust work goes in `crates/` and `apps/`.

Reference: handlers `coder/coderd/*.go`; SDK/API models `coder/codersdk/*.go`; SQL `coder/coderd/database/queries/*.sql`; DB models `coder/coderd/database/*.go`; migrations `coder/coderd/database/migrations/`.

Porting procedure:
1. Find the missing route in `docs/parity-matrix.md`
2. Read the Go handler in `coder/coderd/<file>.go`
3. Read the SDK models in `coder/codersdk/<file>.go`
4. Read the SQL queries in `coder/coderd/database/queries/<file>.sql`
5. Define Rust domain types / API models in `coder-core` or the appropriate feature crate
6. Port storage access and migrations into `coder-db`
7. Port the HTTP handler into `coder-server` (or the appropriate feature crate)
8. Add tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules alongside the code
9. Run validation: `cargo fmt --all && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets && cargo test`

Major unported areas include templates/versions, workspaces/builds, workspace agents, debug/observability, AI tasks, notifications/inbox/webpush, insights, chats, files, params, presets, provisioner jobs, and deprecated routes. Existing crates: `coder-auth`, `coder-identity`, `coder-rbac`, `coder-audit`, `coder-workspaces`, `coder-provisioner`, `coder-connectivity`, `coder-notifications`, `coder-db`, `coder-server`, `coder-core`; `apps/coderd` and `apps/coder-parity`. `coder-server` has 72 handlers; feature crates vary from active to stub.

Stack: Rust edition 2024, MSRV 1.85, toolchain 1.94.0; Axum 0.8; PostgreSQL/sqlx 0.8; Tokio; serde/serde_json; custom API-key/session/PBKDF2 auth; tracing; reqwest/rustls; AGPL-3.0-only.

Key files: `crates/coder-server/src/app.rs`, `crates/coder-server/src/error.rs`, `crates/coder-db/src/store.rs`, `crates/coder-core/src/ports.rs`, `crates/coder-core/src/api.rs`, `crates/coder-core/src/config.rs`, `apps/coderd/src/main.rs`, `docs/parity-matrix.md`, `docs/backend-rewrite.md`. Handlers belong in `crates/coder-server/src/app.rs`; follow existing extractors, JSON responses, and error mapping. Tests belong in `#[cfg(test)]` modules, not separate directories.

cargo run --bin coderd
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
cargo fmt --all
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo run -p coder-parity -- inventory --go-root coder --rust-root . --scope oss --output docs/parity-matrix.md
cargo test -p coder-server

All dependencies are declared in the root `Cargo.toml` under `[workspace.dependencies]`. Crates reference them with `dep.workspace = true`. **Do not** add dependency versions in individual crate `Cargo.toml` files.

The workspace denies `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, and `dbg_macro`, and forbids `unsafe_code`. `unreachable_pub` and `unused_qualifications` warn. Use `thiserror` for error enums and propagate with `?`. Never use `.unwrap()` or `.expect()`.
**No `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` / `panic!()` / `todo!()` / `dbg!()`** — The workspace denies these at the lint level. CI and `cargo clippy` will reject them.
**No `unsafe` code** — Forbidden workspace-wide.
**No per-crate dependency versions** — Always use `workspace = true` references.
**Do not modify files under `coder/`** — This is the vendored Go reference. Treat as read-only.
**Do not create separate `tests/` directories** — Use `#[cfg(test)]` in-file.

1. `cargo fmt --all` — Format all code.
2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — Must pass with zero warnings.
3. `cargo test`
